locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how keys are assigned to nodes on the ring? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: When a key hashes past the highest virtual node, a consistent-hash ring must wrap around to the first vnode (index 0). locate() instead returns the last vnode. Placement is still deterministic, but the arc above the last point is owned by the wrong node, so adding or removing nodes moves those keys inconsistently with the intended ring and skews load toward whichever node owns the highest point.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A user follows 500 authors spread across 6 feed nodes. How many calls to recentPosts does homeTimeline make?
choices: 1, to the node owning the user's id
At most 6, one per distinct node owning any followed author
Always exactly 6, one per node in the cluster
choiceQuestions.explanation: homeTimeline groups followed authors by the node returned from locate() and issues one recentPosts call per group, so it is bounded by the number of distinct owning nodes (at most 6, possibly fewer). It does not call per author, does not route by the reader's id, and skips nodes that own none of the followed authors.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does each node get 128 virtual points instead of one?
choices: To spread each node's ownership across many small arcs so load is more even and a node's removal spreads its keys over many survivors
To store 128 replicas of every post for durability
So that locate() can be O(1)
To allow keys to be routed to 128 nodes in parallel
choiceQuestions.explanation: Virtual nodes split each physical node's share of the hash space into many arcs, evening out load and distributing a removed node's keys across the remaining nodes. They are routing points only; no data is replicated, locate() is a binary search (O(log n)), and each key still maps to one node.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Node C is removed via remove('C'). Which posts can homeTimeline no longer find, assuming no data is moved?
choices: None; the ring re-sorts and finds them elsewhere
Posts by every author, since all routing changes
Only posts published after the removal
Posts previously written to C, because their authors now route to other nodes that never stored them
choiceQuestions.explanation: remove() only drops C's vnodes. Authors that hashed to C now locate() to another node, and recentPosts is sent there, but their earlier posts still live only on C. Other authors' routing is unchanged, so not everything breaks, and new posts would be found because they are written to the new owner.
